full_judgment: 8. The next contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner is that the Election Tribunal in presence of the Advocate of both the parties checked and counted the ballots and found 94 invalid ballots which were fraudulently credited in favour of the opposite party No. I. It is submitted that the learned District Judge illegally discarded the said decision of the Election Tribunal. He, however, conceded that the learned Election Tribunal did not assign any reason for treating those 94 ballots as invalid ones. Clause (b) of Sub-rule (3) of Rule 38 of the Union Parishad (Election) Rules, 1983 provides that the ballots which bear no official mark, or any writing or any mark other than the official mark, or any mark madewith any stamp other than the rubber stamp supplied or the purpose, or to which a piece of paper or another object of any kind has been attached, or no mark with the rubber stamp indicating the contestingcandidate for whom the Voter has Voted, or any markfrom which it is not clear for whom the voter hasvoted, or more marks than the number of contestingcandidates to be elected arc to be treated as invalid ballot papers. In his Judgment, the learned ElectionTribunal did not assign any of the aforesaid reasons for treating 94 ballots as invalid. The learned Advocate for the petitioner argued that when the recounting was done in presence of the Advocates of the parties, no objection was raised against those 94 ballots. I, however, do not find any force in this argumentwhen the learned District Judge himself checked upthose invalid ballot papers and found marks of interpolation. thereon. According to the learned District Judge the interpolation was done after counting of theballots made by the Presiding Officer. It is pointed out by the learned District Judge that the bags con-wining the ballot papers received by the Tribunal had indistinct seals. The order dated 30.4.84 of the Election Tribunal Case shows that the Election Tribunal received 3 bags with indistinct seals. On that it was notedÒ3 (wZb) e¨vM A®úó wmjMvjv Kiv Qvjvi e¯—v eywSqvcvBjvg|This remark clearly indicated that some ballot papers were tampered with after declaration of the result of the election. Such being the position, I hold that the learned District Judge rightly held that the Election Tribunal arbitrarily and without assigning any reason illegally declared 94 ballots as invalid votes. Accordingly I hold that this court in its provisional jurisdiction cannot disturb the finding of the court of appeal below on this question of fact. So I find no substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
